title: Quantum tree networks: complete semidefinite hierarchies and the source-transfer model
authors: Xiangling Xu, Igor Klep, Marc-Olivier Renou
abstract: Understanding the capabilities and limits of quantum systems is central to quantum information processing. This includes determining which correlations can arise in networks of quantum systems distributed by independent sources. Yet for general quantum networks, no systematic, dimension-free method is known to bound these correlations arbitrarily well. We resolve this problem for all quantum tree networks through a new source-transfer model, which we prove equivalent to a mixed quantum model. The mixed model places no restriction on dimension and reduces to the standard tensor-product model in finite dimensions; the source-transfer model instead describes these correlations through states on $C^*$-algebras and completely positive maps composed recursively along the tree. We prove the equivalence by reconstructing local measurements as Radon-Nikodym derivatives in the spatial tensor products prescribed by the network. Building on this characterization, we establish two convergent outer hierarchies of semidefinite programs (SDPs): a novel source-transfer hierarchy and the inflation-NPA hierarchy. For the source-transfer hierarchy, we extend noncommutative real algebraic geometry to multi-state polynomials with completely positive maps, prove a reconstruction theorem establishing its convergence, and give a sufficient stopping criterion for extracting finite-dimensional realizations. For the inflation-NPA hierarchy, we reconstruct source-transfer realizations from weak-operator limits of averages over source copies. Consequently, the game-value promise problem for quantum tree networks in the mixed model is $\mathsf{coRE}$-complete.
summary: This paper develops a comprehensive mathematical framework to characterize correlations in quantum tree networks, resolving the difficulty of finding dimension-free bounds. It introduces the source-transfer model, proving its equivalence to the mixed quantum model, and establishes two complete SDP hierarchies for bounding these correlations. This work advances the theory of quantum correlations beyond simple tensor product assumptions.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of finding a systematic, dimension-free method to bound correlations achievable in general quantum networks, specifically quantum tree networks.
main_result: The authors introduce and prove the equivalence of the novel source-transfer model and the mixed quantum model for tree networks, establishing two complete outer SDP hierarchies for bounding these correlations.
method: The methodology involves developing and proving the completeness of two specialized Semidefinite Programming (SDP) hierarchies—the source-transfer and inflation-NPA hierarchies—using advanced mathematical tools like noncommutative real algebraic geometry and completely positive maps.
model_or_system: The focus is on quantum tree networks, which generalize the Bell scenario. The correlations are characterized by the Mixed Quantum Model ($	ext{C}_{	ext{mix}}$) and formalized using the Source-Transfer Model, which employs $C^*$-algebras and recursive completely positive maps.
key_observables: The game-value promise problem for quantum tree networks in the mixed model, and the convergence of the SDP hierarchies to the true correlation set.
important_parameters: The structure of the network (tree topology), the dimension of the local measurements, and the number of parties involved.
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is that the correlation set is governed by the source-transfer model, which is shown to be equivalent to the mixed quantum model. A key limitation overcome is that simple measurement factorization is insufficient.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the hierarchy progression from Bell scenarios to quantum tree networks using the source-transfer and inflation-NPA hierarchies. Figure 2 compares the mathematical structure of the Mixed vs. Source-Transfer models for a line-of-four network.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first defining the physical problem (bounding correlations in tree networks), then introducing the source-transfer model as the necessary formalism, proving its equivalence to the mixed model, and finally establishing the completeness of the corresponding SDP hierarchies.
why_interesting: The rigorous mathematical characterization of quantum correlations in complex network structures provides fundamental tools for understanding resource theories in quantum information, applicable to quantum communication and computation protocols.

figures.caption: Figure 1: From Bell scenarios to quantum tree networks. Squares denote parties and circles denote independent sources. Dashed contours illustrate outer approximations, with arrows indicating convergence. In (a), the NPA hierarchy converges from outside to the commuting-operator set Cqc, which in general strictly contains Cqa, the closure of finite-dimensional tensor-product correlations. In (b), the source-transfer and inflation-NPA hierarchies both converge from outside to the nonconvex mixed-model correlation set Cmix on tree networks.

Figure 2: Two quantum models for the line-of-four network. Squares denote parties and circles denote independent sources. In the mixed model, local measurements act on the source systems. In the source-transfer model, arrows indicate the recursive evaluation of the correlation from party 1 towards the root at party 4.

Figure 3: Quantum inflation of the line-of-four network with two copies of each source. Squares denote parties and circles denote independent source copies. Colored indices and edges indicate the source copies on which each measurement acts.

Figure 4: A source-party tree with parties 1, . . . , 5 represented by squares and independent sources α1, . . . , α4 represented by circles. The source α2 is tripartite and is shared by parties 2, 3, 4, while α1 and α3 are bipartite. The source α4 is a local source connected only to party 3. In the mixed model of definition 2.1, each source αj carries a Hilbert space Hαj and a unit vector Ωαj . For every adjacent party i ∈NT(αj), the von Neumann algebra Mi αj ⊂B � Hαj  describes the observables of party i on source αj; for each fixed source, these algebras mutually commute. The local observable algebras are M1 = M1 α1, M2 = M2 α1 ⊗M2 α2, M3 = M3 α2 ⊗M3 α3 ⊗M3 α4, M4 = M4 α2, and M5 = M5...

Figure 5: Source-transfer descriptions of two quantum tree networks. Circles denote sources, squares denote parties, and blue squares denote roots. Each source α carries a state ωα on the joint source algebra Aα, formed from the algebras Av α of its child parties. The input algebra of a party v is Ain v = Nmax α∈ch(v) Aα. Leaf parties carry POVM elements, internal non-root parties carry transfer maps, and root parties carry positive functionals. Arrows indicate the direction of transfer toward the root.
